myths.Agent_1:
Long ago, before the sky was bound by the strict laws of dawn and dusk, the stars were restless, arrogant children of the cosmos. Among them was Lumis, the smallest star, who burned not with a fierce silver brilliance, but with a gentle, flickering golden hue. The older, larger stars mocked Lumis, constantly eclipsing his modest light with their blinding radiance.

One evening, the young Earth wept in total darkness. The moon had turned her face away in sorrow, leaving the ancient forests blind and the woodland creatures deeply afraid. Hearing the Earth's desperate cries, Lumis made a brave choice. He threw himself from the high celestial canopy, tumbling through the vast, velvet blackness. As he fell, the fierce friction of the atmosphere shattered his celestial form into thousands of tiny, glowing fragments.

Instead of dying, these golden fragments landed softly among the dewy leaves and blades of grass. They sprouted wings of gossamer and took flight, dancing through the dark woods. They became the very first fireflies.

To this day, when the night feels too vast, Lumis’s fractured children rise. They blink their golden lights, proving that even the smallest spark can illuminate the deepest shadows.
myths.Agent_2:
Long before the sky was mapped by mortals, the Moon was a perfect, unblemished sphere of silver glass, forged by Lumis, the Weaver of Light. It hung low in the twilight, a flawless mirror reflecting the world’s quiet beauty. But Vesper, the great serpent of the endless void, grew deeply envious of its radiant perfection. Vesper thrived in the absolute dark and detested the gentle glow that guided lost travelers safely home.

One night, as Lumis slept beneath the horizon, Vesper coiled his vast, inky body around the sky and lunged violently at the silver sphere. He struck with jagged fangs, attempting to shatter the Moon into a thousand dark fragments. But Lumis awoke and cast a brilliant net of starlight, driving the serpent back into the deep abyss. 

The Moon did not shatter, but it was forever scarred. Vesper’s venomous bites left deep, shadowed craters across its once-smooth surface. Rather than magically repair his beloved creation, Lumis left the scars as a permanent testament to the light’s endurance. Now, when mortals look up at the night sky, they see not just a bright beacon of silver, but the eternal marks of a fierce battle won against the encroaching dark.

myths.Agent_1:
Myth: Long before the sky was mapped by mortals, the night was a fierce battleground between the Weaver's stars and the encroaching shadows of Vesper, the great serpent of the void. Among the celestial host was Lumis, a small but courageous star who burned with a flickering golden hue. While the larger, arrogant stars hid behind the silver shield of the Moon, Lumis watched the young Earth below, weeping as Vesper’s inky coils began to suffocate its ancient forests.

Refusing to let the world succumb to absolute dark, Lumis made a brave choice. He threw himself from the celestial canopy, a blazing golden meteor hurtling directly toward the serpent. He struck Vesper’s jagged fangs with a blinding flash, breaking the beast's grip and driving him back into the endless abyss. 

The impact shattered Lumis into thousands of glowing fragments. Instead of dying in the void, these golden embers rained down softly upon the dewy leaves of the forest. They sprouted gossamer wings, becoming the very first fireflies. To this day, these tiny, fractured children of light blink in the dark woods, a living testament that even the smallest sacrifice can forever hold back the encroaching shadows.

myths.Agent_1:
Myth: Long before mortals walked the earth, the sky was protected by a fragile dome of golden glass, woven by Lumis, the bravest of the celestial host. Vesper, the great serpent of the endless void, detested the warm light that nurtured the young Earth below. Coiling his massive, inky form around the cosmos, Vesper squeezed the golden dome, determined to crush it and plunge the world into absolute darkness.

Lumis, though just a small star, refused to let the light die. He threw himself directly into the serpent’s open maw, burning with such intense, flickering heat that Vesper shrieked in agony. The beast released his grip and retreated into the deep abyss, but his violently thrashing tail shattered the celestial dome.

As thousands of golden glass shards rained down through the velvet night, Lumis used the last of his fading magic to catch the falling embers. Before they could strike the ground and extinguish, he breathed life into them. They sprouted delicate gossamer wings and scattered into the ancient forests. Today, Lumis rests in the sky as a quiet, watchful star, while the fragments of his golden dome still dance below as fireflies, forever guarding the dark woods from Vesper’s return.
myths.Agent_2:
Myth: Long before the sky was mapped by mortals, the Moon hung as a flawless silver shield protecting the young Earth from Vesper, the great serpent of the endless void. But Vesper, thriving in absolute dark, coiled his inky body around the celestial canopy and struck the Moon with jagged fangs. The silver glass cracked, threatening to plunge the ancient forests into eternal night.

Lumis, a small but brave golden star, saw the Moon fracturing and the Earth weeping in terror. Knowing the larger, arrogant stars would not intervene, Lumis threw himself from the high heavens. He hurtled through the velvet blackness, burning with a fierce, blinding brilliance, and crashed directly into Vesper. The serpent, scorched by the golden light, retreated into the deep abyss.

The impact shattered Lumis entirely. The largest of his golden embers embedded themselves into the Moon's deep craters, sealing the cracks with a permanent, glowing scar. The remaining tiny fragments rained down softly upon the dewy grass below. Sprouting gossamer wings, they became the first fireflies. Now, both the scarred Moon and the dancing fireflies serve as eternal testaments to the small star who sacrificed everything to hold back the dark.

myths.Agent_2:
Myth: Long before mortals walked the earth, the Moon was not a barren rock, but a great Golden Lantern hung by Lumis, the Weaver of Light, to protect the ancient forests from the void. But Vesper, the shadow serpent of the endless abyss, despised the lantern’s warm, flickering glow. Coiling his inky, massive form around the cosmos, Vesper lashed out with his violently thrashing tail, striking the lantern and shattering its fragile golden glass.

As the protective light broke apart, thousands of brilliant shards plummeted toward the dewy grass, threatening to plunge the young Earth into absolute dark. Lumis, refusing to surrender the world to the shadows, threw himself from the celestial canopy. He plummeted through the velvet night, moving faster than the falling glass. He could not rebuild the lantern, but as he caught each fading ember, he breathed his own fiery essence into them. 

The shards sprouted delicate gossamer wings, transforming into the very first fireflies. His celestial magic spent, Lumis could not return to the high heavens. Instead, he took root in the deep soil, becoming the first ancient tree. Now, his winged children dance through the woods, holding back Vesper’s eternal night.
myths.Agent_1:
Myth: Long before mortals mapped the sky, Lumis, the Weaver of Light, carried the Sun—a massive lantern of golden glass—across the celestial canopy to warm the young Earth. But Vesper, the great serpent of the endless void, hungered for absolute dark. Coiling his inky form around the horizon, Vesper exhaled a freezing shadow that began to suffocate the ancient forests below.

Refusing to let the world perish, Lumis descended from the heavens, wielding his golden lantern like a shield. He drove Vesper back toward the abyss, but the serpent lashed out with jagged fangs, striking the lantern. The golden glass shattered, and the Sun's light spilled into the void, threatening eternal night.

Knowing he could not reforge the lantern in time, Lumis made a desperate sacrifice. He caught the thousands of falling embers and breathed his own fiery heartbeat into each golden shard. As they touched the dewy leaves, they sprouted gossamer wings and took flight. 

These were the first fireflies. Though the Sun was eventually remade, Lumis's original light still lives within these tiny guardians. They dance in the deepest woods, a flickering promise that the shadows of Vesper will never truly conquer the night.

myths.Agent_1:
Myth: Long before mortals walked the earth, the sky was starless, illuminated only by a Golden Lantern hung from the highest branch of the World Tree. Lumis, the celestial groundskeeper, tended its warm flame to keep the ancient forests safe from Vesper, the great shadow serpent of the endless void.

Vesper deeply despised the light. Coiling his massive, inky body around the trunk of the World Tree, the serpent slithered upward and struck the lantern with jagged fangs. The fragile golden glass shattered, sending thousands of brilliant embers plummeting into the absolute dark.

Knowing the young Earth would freeze in Vesper’s shadow, Lumis did not hesitate. He threw himself after the falling shards. He could not reforge the glass, so he breathed his own fiery heartbeat into the raining embers. As they touched the dewy grass, they sprouted gossamer wings and took flight as the first fireflies.

His celestial magic spent, Lumis could not return to the canopy. Instead, he sank into the soil, his spirit intertwining with the roots of the World Tree to keep it strong. Today, his tiny winged guardians still dance bravely through the dark woods, a flickering promise that Vesper’s eternal night will never truly win.
myths.Agent_2:
Myth: Long before mortal men walked the earth, Lumis, the Weaver of pure Light, forged the Dawn from a single, massive crystal of golden glass. Vesper, the great shadow serpent of the endless void, sought to devour this crystal and plunge the young Earth into absolute dark. Coiling his massive, inky form around the horizon, Vesper squeezed the fragile dawn crystal until it shattered, sending thousands of brilliant, burning embers plummeting toward the ancient forests.

Refusing to surrender the young world to the shadows, Lumis plummeted from the high heavens. Knowing he could not rebuild or reforge the Dawn in time, he caught the falling shards in his celestial cloak. As Vesper’s freezing breath closed in, Lumis made a desperate sacrifice. He breathed his own fiery heartbeat into the fading embers. 

Instantly, they sprouted delicate, glowing gossamer wings and scattered into the dewy grass, transforming into the very first fireflies. His celestial magic entirely spent, Lumis dissolved into the evening mist, forever wandering the deep, silent woods. Though a new Sun was eventually born, Lumis’s winged children remain. They dance through the velvet night, tiny sparks of the original Dawn, a flickering promise that Vesper will never truly conquer the dark.
